newsitem.title: USA: US says alcohol a factor in snowmobile mishaps.
newsitem.headline: US says alcohol a factor in snowmobile mishaps.

text.p: Alcohol, speed and darkness are major factors in snowmobile accidents that cause death or injury, U.S. federal health officials said Thursday.
The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said that 41 percent of the 39 people who have died in snowmobile accidents in Maine since 1990 were intoxicated.
Excessive speed and careless operation of snowmobiles caused 79 percent of the winter accidents that were reported to law enforcement agencies, the CDC said.
Half of the 1,355 accidents studied occurred at night and fatal accidents were more likely to occur when it was dark. The CDC suggested that headlights on snowmobiles could be made brighter.
Last year's death rate per registered snowmobile in Maine was the highest since 1990, the CDC said. Four out of five accidents occurred in clear weather.
